title: Candied walnuts
subtitle: walnuts in a crisp, sweet, lightly spiced caramel shell
excerpt: Candied walnuts take about fifteen minutes from start to finish. The walnuts are tossed in a sugar syrup on the hob and spread onto a lined tray to set. The result is individually coated nuts with a crisp, glassy shell. They keep for three weeks in a tin and are useful for cakes, salads, and cheese boards as well as eating on their own.
sourceNotes: Candied nut confectionery documented in British and American household cookbooks from the early twentieth century. Technique is consistent across multiple sources.

glossaryTerms.definition: Nuts coated in or embedded in caramelised sugar. When the sugar cools and sets, the result is either left as a brittle slab or ground to a paste.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 3 weeks. Do not refrigerate.

content.text: Candied walnuts are a form of

where the nuts stay separate rather than being cast as a slab. The trick is to stir constantly over the heat and then spread the nuts immediately onto a lined tray so they separate as the sugar sets around each one.
Line a baking tray with a baking mat or lightly oiled baking parchment and set it near the hob.
Put the sugar and water into a medium saucepan over a medium-high heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves, then let the syrup come to the boil without stirring.

Add the walnuts and cinnamon (if using). Stir continuously with a silicone spatula for 5 to 7 minutes over a medium heat. The syrup will look crystallised and dry for a minute, then begin to re-melt to a clear caramel. Keep stirring until all the walnuts are coated in a golden caramel shell.
Tip immediately onto the prepared tray and use two forks or the spatula to separate the walnuts from each other before the caramel sets. Sprinkle with flaky salt if using.
Leave to cool for 20 minutes until fully set and crisp. The nuts should have a glassy shell. Store in an airtight tin at room temperature.

attrs.avoid: Avoid leaving them on the tray without separating immediately after pouring.
attrs.fix: Work quickly with two forks to break clumps apart as soon as the nuts hit the tray; the caramel sets within 2 minutes.

attrs.avoid: Avoid cooking at too high a temperature; the sugar continues to cook in the pan after the nuts are added.
attrs.fix: Keep the heat at medium once the nuts go in and stir constantly to prevent hot spots.
